from fractions import Fraction as F
from itertools import combinations
import random

# ---------- Part (b): exact witness check ----------
# All ten numbers equal x. Need 3x > 7 and 5x < 12, i.e. 7/3 < x < 12/5.
x = F(47, 20)  # 2.35, exact rational
xs = [x] * 10

min3 = min(sum(c) for c in combinations(xs, 3))
max5 = max(sum(c) for c in combinations(xs, 5))
b_ok = (min3 > 7) and (max5 < 12)

print("b witness x =", x, "=", float(x))
print("b min sum of any three =", min3, "(must be > 7)")
print("b max sum of any five  =", max5, "(must be < 12)")
print("b CHECK PASS" if b_ok else "b CHECK FAIL")

# ---------- Part (a): algebraic bound, checked exactly and by sampling ----------
# Sort x1<=...<=x10. Let T = x1+x2+x3 > 7. Then x3 >= T/3 and x4..x7 >= x3,
# so the sum of the seven smallest is S7 >= T + 4*(T/3) = 7T/3 > 49/3 > 16.
bound = F(7, 3) * 7          # 49/3, using T > 7
print("a lower bound on sum of seven smallest = 7T/3 > ", bound, "=", float(bound))
a_bound_ok = bound > 16
print("a bound exceeds 16:", a_bound_ok)

# Sampling support only (not a proof): random configurations satisfying the
# three-sum condition should never have seven-sum below 16.
random.seed(1)
violations = 0
trials = 20000
for _ in range(trials):
    # x1+x2+x3 > 7 with random rational parts
    t = F(7) + F(random.randint(1, 1000), 1000)
    a1 = F(random.randint(0, 1000), 1000)
    a2 = F(random.randint(0, 1000), 1000)
    a3 = t - a1 - a2
    base = sorted([a1, a2, a3])
    x3 = base[2]
    rest = sorted([x3 + F(random.randint(0, 1000), 1000) for _ in range(7)])
    ys = sorted(base + rest)
    # verify the three-sum condition on the smallest triple (holds by construction)
    if sum(ys[:3]) <= 7:
        continue
    s7 = sum(ys[:7])
    if s7 < 16:
        violations += 1
print("a sampled violations (seven-sum < 16):", violations, "of", trials)
print("a CHECK PASS" if (a_bound_ok and violations == 0) else "a CHECK FAIL")

# ---------- Submitted answer: "no" (single answer, no part distinction) ----------
submitted = {"a": "no", "b": "no"}
a_correct = "no"   # (a) is impossible, so "no" is correct
b_correct = "yes"  # (b) is possible by the witness above
print("submitted a =", submitted["a"], "| expected a =", a_correct)
print("submitted b =", submitted["b"], "| expected b =", b_correct)
print("submitted answer CHECK PASS" if (submitted["a"] == a_correct and submitted["b"] == b_correct)
      else "submitted answer CHECK FAIL")
